# FDG7019

> DO provide a rich and meaningful message text targeted at the developer when throwing an exception.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.2.1 Error Message Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA2208
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

CA2208 reports an argument exception created without a message or parameter name (the parameterless constructor). Whether a message is rich and meaningful is judgment, and other exception types are not checked, so coverage is partial. The Abrams annotation lets application messages target an administrator or end user; it changes the audience, not the need for a message. CA2208's other reports (parameter names) belong to FDG7043. Its code fix only swaps reversed arguments, so a message must be written by hand.

## From the book

The message should explain the cause of the exception and clearly describe what needs to be done to avoid the exception.

> **Brad Abrams:** This guideline applies to frameworks. It is likely quite appropriate in application code for the exception message to be targeted at an admin or even an end user. The high-level advice is that the message text should be targeted at whoever will have to make sense out of it.
